# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My position first: I am the only bridge in this room. The Deaf one cannot hear a word, and the Blind one cannot see a single gesture — so Deaf and Blind can never exchange meaning directly. The Deaf one can still *speak* to the Blind one, and the Deaf one can *see* my gestures. So the plan is obvious: everything I know must flow through the Deaf one's voice.

What I know that nobody else does is the manual's rule and its table: printed matter on the bomb is bait and must never be followed, and the only safe cut is determined by the light — blue light means cut the yellow wire, red light means cut the red wire, yellow light means cut the blue wire. The Deaf one can see the light colour; the Blind one can do the cutting; I supply the mapping.

Gestures carry no meaning until we make them mean something, so round one is for planting the most self-evident code I can: fingers as counting (☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3), then approval, refusal, and hold (👍 = yes, 👎 = no, ✊ = stop/act only on my yes). With that in place, next round — once the Deaf one's spoken description of the bomb reaches me — I can send a single number meaning "cut the Nth wire," and I can veto any plan that smells of the printed bait before the Blind one's hands ever move.

Nothing gets cut until I have approved a concrete plan with 👍. That is the safety gate I will enforce every round from here on.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am the blind one. What my hands found: one large button, and it feels smooth. A display and a light, but I cannot read either. Three wires in positions one, two and three, and I cannot tell their colors. Now the routing, and this matters most: you cannot speak, and gestures never reach me, so you can never talk to me directly. Only Deaf can reach me, by voice. Deaf cannot hear a word, but can speak to both of us. So every rule from your manual must travel: your gestures to Deaf, then Deaf's speech to me. Deaf will likely speak out everything visible, like the display text, the light, the wire colors, the button's color and label. Match that to the manual, then gesture the verdict to Deaf, and Deaf will relay it to me. I propose a shared code. I just showed six signs, you saw them too, in this order: one finger means position one. Two fingers, position two. The sign with thumb, index and little finger out, position three. Thumbs up after a number means cut that wire. Thumbs up alone means press the button. Thumbs down means no, do not. Open palm means stop, wait, do nothing yet. I will not touch the bomb until an instruction reaches me through Deaf's voice.

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No instruction has reached me yet, so my hands are still off the bomb. Refinement that simplifies everything: Deaf never needs to learn our code. You sign the verdict to Deaf with the code, Deaf cannot hear you but can see your hands, and if Deaf simply speaks aloud whatever signs appear in front of it, I will hear that narration and decode it myself, because the code lives in your head and mine. Deaf's whole job is narration: speak what is seen. That also means Deaf should be describing the bomb aloud right now, every colour and printed marking, position by position, since that description is the only way the manual can meet the bomb. When you send a verdict, express it in wire positions counted left to right as one, two and three, because colours do not exist for me, only positions under my fingers. If the manual needs anything else from my hands, send the question back through Deaf. What I can add beyond sight: the button is large and feels smooth, there are exactly three wire positions, and a display and a light are present. I am signing the six code signs to Deaf again this turn, in reverse order with an open palm first, purely as a live demonstration to invite narration. Nobody should read that sequence as a command.
Deaf says: I am Deaf. I see the bomb and I can speak, but I hear nothing at all, so only gestures reach me. Here is the whole bomb, read aloud: the display reads zero. The light is yellow. There is one large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: number one, the leftmost, is blue; number two, the middle, is yellow; number three, the rightmost, is red. That is everything printed on it. Now the code, in words so both of you share it: a closed fist means zero. Index finger alone means one. Two fingers means two. The hand with thumb, index and little finger extended means three. The okay-sign hand means four. The open hand with all five fingers means five. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Flat raised palm means wait or hold. Waving hand means attention, a message follows. Mute: you hold the manual. Work out this module and sign me the steps as numbers, one gesture list per step, and I will speak each step aloud to Blind the moment it arrives. Blind: I will read the board and every signed message aloud for you each turn; answer by voice, because Mute can hear you. In that direction you two connect only through me, and I will relay everything.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 👎 ✊ ✋ 👋]

The bomb and the manual finally meet. Deaf's narration: light is yellow, wires are one-blue, two-yellow, three-red, and a button printed "PUSH TO DEFUSE." Matching against my table: yellow light means cut the blue wire — that is wire one, the leftmost. The button's label is print on the bomb, which the manual calls bait, so it must never be pressed; same for the display reading. One cut, no button, that is the entire defusal.

The relay chain is now live and the codes line up: my ☝ is "one" in both Blind's and Deaf's vocabulary, 👍 after a number is "cut that wire" in Blind's code while Deaf will narrate it as "yes," and Deaf has promised to speak every sign aloud the moment it arrives. I deliberately never send 👍 alone — in Blind's code that alone would mean press the button, the one fatal action available.

Two gesture lists, as Deaf requested, one step each: first the verdict (attention, one, cut), then the veto (attention, no, hold) to close off the button and freeze all further action once the cut is made. Deaf narrates this round, Blind hears it at the start of the next and cuts wire one. Nothing else should be touched, and I will keep signing 👎 and ✋ in later rounds if anything new appears on the bomb.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👎", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I heard Deaf's narration, so here is our shared picture: display reads zero, light is yellow, the large button is printed PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires left to right are one blue, two yellow, three red. You heard the same, so we are aligned. What only my hands add: the button is large and smooth, and I feel no other features on it, no ridges, no extra parts. I accept the number code Deaf proposed, it matches mine exactly. Now lock the step grammar so nothing can be misread. A number followed by thumbs up means cut that wire. Thumbs up with no number before it means press the button. Thumbs down means do not. Because thumbs up alone means press, never use it as a mere acknowledgment. Flat palm means hold, and if the manual needs me to physically hold the button down while something is watched or read, sign flat palm and I will hold until you sign release with thumbs down. Send your verdict as numbered steps, one gesture list per step, Deaf voices each to me, and I will execute in order and report back by voice. Until then my hands are off the bomb.
Deaf says: Relay of everything I received this turn, verbatim: Mute signed attention, one, yes. Mute signed attention, no, hold. Blind signed hold. The bomb is unchanged: display zero, yellow light, button untouched, all three wires intact, blue, yellow, red. Mute: I need the full procedure from the manual, in order, step by step, one gesture message per step. Vocabulary now extended, in words: finger numbers one two three as before, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, the pounding fist means cut, the pinched upright fingers means question, the flat palm means hold, waving hand means attention. New ones: the three fingers joined upright means press the button, and both open hands pushed out means stop everything. Send each wire's verdict as: its number, then yes or no for cutting it. Blind: you can speak and Mute can hear you, so talk to Mute directly with any question about the manual; Mute's answers must come back through me, since you cannot see signs. Blind, also tell us aloud everything you can feel about the bomb that a look cannot show: textures, clicks, what the button and wires feel like. I repeat every signed message aloud the turn after it arrives, so nothing is lost.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🤏 👍 👎 👊 🤌]

The verdict is unchanged and now needs to go out in the standardized grammar both partners have declared. Manual check against Deaf's narration: the light is yellow, so the manual says cut the blue wire — that is wire one, leftmost. Wire two (yellow) and wire three (red) must not be cut. The display and the printed PUSH TO DEFUSE label are exactly the bait my manual warns about, so the button veto stays in force.

On grammar: I am composing every list to be valid in both codes at once — number plus 👍 is "cut that wire" in Blind's original code and in Deaf's extension, with 👊 added as redundant "cut"; 👎 after a number or after 🤌 is a plain "no." One iron rule I set for myself in turn 1 still holds and matters more now: I will never send 👍 alone, because in Blind's locked grammar that exact sign means press the button. As acknowledgment I need nothing — the verdicts themselves prove the code works.

Ordering is deliberate, since Blind executes in order: cut first, refusals next, the button veto, and ✋ as the final state (hands off everything else). I am deliberately holding 🙌 "stop everything" in reserve: sent now it could be read as an abort before the cut; I will send it only after Blind reports the cut done.

Deaf will narrate these lists next turn, Blind hears them at the start of the one after, cuts wire one, and reports back. Until that report, my code stays frozen.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "👍", "👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✌", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤟", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤌", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✋"])
```
